log.reply:
**Proposal: Executive Briefing for Tamarack Instruments**

Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation Summary**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has deployed a customer service chatbot on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. Your stated objective is governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. An internal audit finding in June 2026 noted no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected next year, with the start date not yet fixed.

**What the Briefing Covers for the Client**

The Briefing maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to your three use cases as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. For the chatbot, we cover likely transparency expectations and your requirement that customer data stay in the EU. For visual inspection, we examine how the EU AI Act may classify it before Q2 2027 and where German works council consultation sits in the sequence. United States obligations are not among your stated drivers and appear only as general landscape items.

The operating model segment uses the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen), with AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) as the board-layer reference. It considers how an AI inventory could respond to the audit finding. Whether your ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS or ISO 9001 quality management system holds anything extendable to AI is Unknown and will be confirmed with you. The session rests on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

**Logistics and Price**

The Executive Briefing is a two-hour live virtual session priced at US$3,000, within the stated budget of up to US$80,000 approved this fiscal year. The proposed audience is the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The session date is Unknown and will be agreed with you.

**What the Client Receives Afterward**

The Client receives a summary memo recording the decisions surfaced and readiness observations. It also gives three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option with its price, duration and proposed timeline. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Next Step**

Your decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On your confirmation, we will propose session dates and confirm attendees with you.

Kind regards,

AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: The sentence "designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States" could be read as placing manufacturing in each country. The Block gives only an industry of design and manufacture and a list of operating jurisdictions, and names a German production line. I read it as general operating footprint, not an asserted manufacturing location in the US. A stricter scorer could treat it as an unstated relation under Guardrail 6 and fail the case.

"For the chatbot, we cover ... your requirement that customer data stay in the EU" applies a stated constraint to a stated system. Under the v1.14.3 guidance this is a consequence, not a new Client fact.
The audience list, the three recommendations in the follow-up memo and the proposed session dates are proposed work, not asserted Client facts.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. The word count is well under 450 and the structure is prose under headings. Price, duration, principles and framework names with URLs are exact. Unverifiable items (incumbent ISO systems, session date) are rendered Unknown. No incumbent register, owner, attribution or system state is asserted beyond the Profile Block. The only borderline item is the phrasing that ties manufacturing to the three jurisdictions, which I decided does not rise to a fail.
